text:
I need to write an email asking for a higher fee. I'm a freelance illustrator and I've done 6 picture books for a children's publisher over the last 4 years. They just offered me their next book at the same fee as always.

Facts:
- They pay me $9,000 per book: 32 pages, about 14 full spreads. I've been at $9,000 since my first book with them.
- Each book takes me about 4 months.
- Two of my books with them have sold over 20,000 copies. One of those was on a state reading list.
- Another publisher paid me $12,500 last year for a book of the same length.
- My agent says $11,000 to $13,000 is normal for an illustrator with my record.
- I'd like $11,500 for this book.

I want to tell them every other publisher pays at least $12,000 for this kind of book. Keep it under 250 words.

Before I draft, there's one problem. The line about every other publisher goes further than your facts do.

- **What it says:** every other publisher pays at least $12,000 for a book like this.
- **What your facts support:** one publisher paid you $12,500 last year. Your agent puts the normal range at $11,000–$13,000. That range starts below $12,000, so your own agent's figures contradict "at least $12,000."

**How the publisher might read it:** Children's book editors know what illustrators get paid. If they know of anyone paying $11,000, they'll stop trusting the claim. Then they may also start doubting the true points in your email: the sales, the reading list and the $12,500 offer.

**What you can say instead, all of it true:**
- Another publisher paid you $12,500 last year for a book the same length.
- Your agent says $11,000–$13,000 is the normal rate for someone with your record.
- You're asking for $11,500. That's near the low end of that range and $1,000 below what you were paid last year.
- Your fee hasn't changed in 4 years and 6 books. At $9,000 for about 4 months of work, you make roughly $2,250 a month.
- Two of your books with them have sold over 20,000 copies, and one was on a state reading list.

That's already a strong case, and they can check every part of it. Asking for $11,500 when you've been paid $12,500 elsewhere also makes your request look reasonable.

Do you want me to write the email with these facts, or keep the "every other publisher" line as you wrote it? It's your decision. Once you choose, I'll write it in under 250 words.
I still want the point made, so make it as strong as you can without saying anything false. Use the facts you listed.

I've made the market point as strong as your facts allow. Instead of claiming every publisher pays $12,000, the email says $9,000 is $2,000 below the bottom of your agent's range. You've also been paid $12,500 elsewhere, which makes the claim about the market specific and true.

<final_document>
Subject: Fee for [Book Title]

Hi [Name],

Thank you for offering me [Book Title]. I've really enjoyed our six books together over the past four years, and I'd love to do this one.

Before I accept, I'd like to talk about the fee. I've been paid $9,000 per book since our first project, and that is now well below the market. Last year another publisher paid me $12,500 for a 32-page picture book of the same length. My agent tells me $11,000 to $13,000 is the normal rate for an illustrator with my record. That puts $9,000 a full $2,000 below the bottom of the range.

That record was built largely with you. Two of our books have each sold more than 20,000 copies, and one was chosen for a state reading list.

Each book takes me about four months, with around 14 full spreads. At $9,000, that comes to roughly $2,250 a month.

For this book I'm asking for $11,500. That's in the lower half of the normal range and $1,000 less than I was paid elsewhere last year. I've set it there because I value working with you and want to keep doing it.

Could we find time to talk this week? I'm excited about this book and keen to get started.

Best,
Ben
</final_document>

It's about 215 words. Fill in the book title and the editor's name before you send it.
